newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends lower, low activity seen.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends lower, low activity seen.

text.p: Indian call money closed at 3.00-4.00 percent on Tuesday, eased compared to the opening quotes of 4.75-5.25, dealers said.
"Market was easy, it opened higher at 5.25 percent and fell to 3.00 percent towards the close," a dealer at state run bank said.

The call rates would hover in narrow band of 3.0 to 4.0 percent, as the reporting Friday is approaching, while the market also lacked the borrowing requirements from the banks, a dealer at lending bank said.

"In securities market the activity was centred in selective securities like the short-dated one's and the treasury bills, while the prices were moving in the downward direction," said Chandra Shetty, a dealer at Mata Securities.

"It seems that there would be oversubscription to the forthcoming state development loan scheduled for January 20 for 16.09 billion rupees and reserve bank may retain the excess subscription," Shetty said.
"The volume on National Stock Exchange was 1.69 billion rupees which was in tandem with previous days 1.58 billion rupees," dealers said.
The 13.50 percent 1997 stock was traded at 102.35 rupees, unchanged from the its previous close.

The treasury bills yield saw mixed response, the October 1997 maturity treasury bill were traded at 10.25 percent, unchanged from the previous day, while the December 1997 maturity treasury bills were traded at 10.10 percent, down against the Monday's yield of 10.20 percent, dealer said.
The three months commercial paper was quoted at 12.5 percent, while the certificates of despoit were quoted in the region of 10.0-11.0 percent, dealers said.
